A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same PAID research work and complete, readable 17-page documents, including Appendices A–D. Text comparison and rendering establish that pages 2–17 are identical; differences are confined to first-page author and version information.

before.justification: v1 reports original geometric analyses, classification and segmentation experiments, and ablations in Sections 1 and 4 and Appendices A–D.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original empirical results, including PAID benchmark evaluations, component ablations, and ten-round adaptation results.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same weight decomposition, frozen original directions, chained Householder transformations, and source–target feature-statistics alignment objective.

E1.justification: Both evaluate CIFAR10-C, CIFAR100-C, and ImageNet-C classification and Cityscapes-to-ACDC segmentation. The CIFAR-100 semantic-shift experiment and all appendix evaluation scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within each corresponding experiment, including the CTTA baselines in Tables 1–4 and 9–12 and the LoRA and DoRA comparisons in Table 5.

E3.justification: The backbones, corruption severity, preprocessing, metrics, batch sizes, optimizer settings, and adaptation schedules are unchanged. Both retain three-round segmentation evaluation and the ten-round classification analysis.

E4.justification: The geometric motivation experiments, attention visualizations, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, computational comparison, and long-term adaptation analysis are identical in Section 4.3 and Appendices A–B.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version adds independent-run or seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the same averages across domains and adaptation rounds are retained.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are identical. Tables 1–4 retain PAID errors of 42.2%, 24.9%, and 11.0% on ImageNet-C, CIFAR100-C, and CIFAR10-C, respectively, and 62.2% mIoU on ACDC; appendix results also match exactly.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9, geometric definitions, CTTA assumptions, and the mathematical discussion of orthogonal and Householder transformations are unchanged. No proof, derivation, or formal assumption is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about pairwise angular structure as a domain-invariant semantic prior and PAID's effectiveness across four CTTA benchmarks.

C2.justification: The interpretations of angular preservation, the Fourier analogy, and explanations of ablation findings are identical. Appendix C retains the same limitations concerning applicability under extreme conditions and hyperparameter tuning.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A provide identical implementation and reproducibility information, including hyperparameters, source-statistics preparation, RTX 3090 hardware, and the attention-rollout code reference.

R1.justification: The CTTA and parameter-efficient fine-tuning positioning, including discussion of DoRA and OFT, is unchanged. All 74 references are retained without changes.

P1.justification: The first-page author name changes from 'Yunfei Bao' to 'Yuanfei Bao', and the arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 3 June 2025 to v2 dated 3 July 2025. Scientific prose, terminology, and document structure are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–12 retain identical content, captions, formatting, and placement. The page layout is preserved, with rendered pages 2–17 matching exactly.

improvement.justification: v2 changes only an author-name spelling and the version/date information. The scientific content, empirical support, explanations, reproducibility information, and limitations remain identical throughout the main text and appendices, establishing no meaningful change in overall paper quality.
